32		Args:              cobra.ExactArgs(1),

68	// resolveCreateName folds the -n shorthand into the set map and derives the
69	// output dir. -n is sugar for --set name=<v>; it also defaults --output.
70	func resolveCreateName(name, output string, sets map[string]any) (string, error) {
71		if name == "" {
72			return output, nil
73		}
74		if _, ok := sets["name"]; ok {
75			return "", newUsageErrorf("cannot combine --name with --set name= (they conflict)")
76		}
77		sets["name"] = name
78		if output == "" {
79			output = name
80		}

82	}

256	## Deployment manifests (`intropy manifests`)
257	
258	### Generate Kubernetes manifests
259	
260	Run inside a scaffolded integration (any subdirectory works — the command
261	walks up to find `.intropy/scaffold.json`):
262	
263	```sh
264	intropy manifests create
265	```
266	
267	This re-fetches the blueprint at the exact version pinned in
268	`.intropy/scaffold.json` and renders its `manifests/` templates into a
269	kustomize tree:
270	
271	```
272	deploy/
273	├── base/                  Deployment + Service with Dapr sidecar annotations
274	│   ├── deployment.yaml
275	│   ├── service.yaml
276	│   └── kustomization.yaml
277	└── overlays/
278	    ├── dev/               Dapr components for local-style backends
279	    └── prod/              Real-broker placeholders, secrets via secretKeyRef
280	```
281	
282	Values recorded at scaffold time (like `name` and `appPort`) pre-fill the
283	matching manifest parameters, so you're only asked for what's new — typically
284	the container image:
285	
286	```sh
287	# inline
288	intropy manifests create --set imageRepository=ghcr.io/acme/orders --set imageTag=1.0.0
289	
290	# non-interactive (fail fast on missing required values)
291	intropy manifests create --no-input -f deploy-values.yaml
292	
293	# elsewhere than deploy/, or on top of existing files
294	intropy manifests create -o ./k8s --force
295	
296	# newer blueprint release than the one pinned at scaffold time
297	intropy manifests create --version v1.5.0
298	
299	# machine-readable result document (consumed by chained tooling)
300	intropy manifests create --output-json -
301	```

311	## Skills (`intropy skills`)
312	
313	Skills are stored as OCI artifacts following the
314	[Agent Skills OCI Artifacts Spec](https://github.com/ThomasVitale/agents-skills-oci-artifacts-spec)
315	— config schema, layer layout, and annotations all conform to it, so anything
316	the CLI publishes can be consumed by other spec-compliant clients (and
317	vice-versa). The CLI maintains two files at the project root:
318	
319	- `skills.json` — declares registered collections and installed skills (committed).
320	- `skills.lock.json` — pins resolved digests and install paths (committed).
321	
322	Skills install into `.agents/skills/<name>/` (the canonical layout from §9 of
323	the spec). Additional install locations can be configured per skill via
324	`--also-install-to`.
325	
326	### Add a skill
327	
328	By full OCI reference:
329

332	```

339	```

341	If no `skills.json` exists in the working directory or any parent, an empty one
342	is created in the current directory.

349	```

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/robinhultman/.claude/skills/golang-cli

**Persona:** You are a Go CLI engineer. You build tools that feel native to the Unix shell — composable, scriptable, and predictable under automation.

**Modes:**

- **Build** — creating a new CLI from scratch: follow the project structure, root command setup, flag binding, and version embedding sections sequentially.
- **Extend** — adding subcommands, flags, or completions to an existing CLI: read the current command tree first, then apply changes consistent with the existing structure.
- **Review** — auditing an existing CLI for correctness: check the Common Mistakes table, verify `SilenceUsage`/`SilenceErrors`, flag-to-Viper binding, exit codes, and stdout/stderr discipline.

# Go CLI Best Practices

Use Cobra + Viper as the default stack for Go CLI applications. Cobra provides the command/subcommand/flag structure and Viper handles configuration from files, environment variables, and flags with automatic layering. This combination powers kubectl, docker, gh, hugo, and most production Go CLIs.

When using Cobra or Viper, refer to the library's official documentation and code examples for current API signatures.

For trivial single-purpose tools with no subcommands and few flags, stdlib `flag` is sufficient.

## Quick Reference

| Concern             | Package / Tool                       |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| Commands & flags    | `github.com/spf13/cobra`             |
| Configuration       | `github.com/spf13/viper`             |
| Flag parsing        | `github.com/spf13/pflag` (via Cobra) |
| Colored output      | `github.com/fatih/color`             |
| Table output        | `github.com/olekukonko/tablewriter`  |
| Interactive prompts | `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea` |
| Version injection   | `go build -ldflags`                  |
| Distribution        | `goreleaser`                         |

## Project Structure

Organize CLI commands in `cmd/myapp/` with one file per command. Keep `main.go` minimal — it only calls `Execute()`.

```
myapp/
├── cmd/
│   └── myapp/
│       ├── main.go              # package main, only calls Execute()
│       ├── root.go              # Root command + Viper init
│       ├── serve.go             # "serve" subcommand
│       ├── migrate.go           # "migrate" subcommand
│       └── version.go           # "version" subcommand
├── go.mod
└── go.sum
```

`main.go` should be minimal — see [assets/examples/main.go](assets/examples/main.go).

## Root Command Setup

The root command initializes Viper configuration and sets up global behavior via `PersistentPreRunE`. See [assets/examples/root.go](assets/examples/root.go).

Key points:

- `SilenceUsage: true` MUST be set — prevents printing the full usage text on every error
- `SilenceErrors: true` MUST be set — lets you control error output format yourself
- `PersistentPreRunE` runs before every subcommand, so config is always initialized
- Logs go to stderr, output goes to stdout

## Subcommands

Add subcommands by creating separate files in `cmd/myapp/` and registering them in `init()`. See [assets/examples/serve.go](assets/examples/serve.go) for a complete subcommand example including command groups.

## Flags

See [assets/examples/flags.go](assets/examples/flags.go) for all flag patterns:

### Persistent vs Local

- **Persistent** flags are inherited by all subcommands (e.g., `--config`)
- **Local** flags only apply to the command they're defined on (e.g., `--port`)

### Required Flags

Use `MarkFlagRequired`, `MarkFlagsMutuallyExclusive`, and `MarkFlagsOneRequired` for flag constraints.

### Flag Validation with RegisterFlagCompletionFunc

Provide completion suggestions for flag values.

### Always Bind Flags to Viper

This ensures `viper.GetInt("port")` returns the flag value, env var `MYAPP_PORT`, or config file value — whichever has highest precedence.

## Argument Validation

Cobra provides built-in validators for positional arguments. See [assets/examples/args.go](assets/examples/args.go) for both built-in and custom validation examples.

| Validator                   | Description                          |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `cobra.NoArgs`              | Fails if any args provided           |
| `cobra.ExactArgs(n)`        | Requires exactly n args              |
| `cobra.MinimumNArgs(n)`     | Requires at least n args             |
| `cobra.MaximumNArgs(n)`     | Allows at most n args                |
| `cobra.RangeArgs(min, max)` | Requires between min and max         |
| `cobra.ExactValidArgs(n)`   | Exactly n args, must be in ValidArgs |

## Configuration with Viper

Viper resolves configuration values in this order (highest to lowest precedence):

1. **CLI flags** (explicit user input)
2. **Environment variables** (deployment config)
3. **Config file** (persistent settings)
4. **Defaults** (set in code)

See [assets/examples/config.go](assets/examples/config.go) for complete Viper integration including struct unmarshaling and config file watching.

### Example Config File (.myapp.yaml)

```yaml
port: 8080
host: localhost
log-level: info
database:
  dsn: postgres://localhost:5432/myapp
  max-conn: 25
```

With the setup above, these are all equivalent:

- Flag: `--port 9090`
- Env var: `MYAPP_PORT=9090`
- Config file: `port: 9090`

## Version and Build Info

Version SHOULD be embedded at compile time using `ldflags`. See [assets/examples/version.go](assets/examples/version.go) for the version command and build instructions.

## Exit Codes

Exit codes MUST follow Unix conventions:

| Code  | Meaning           | When to Use                               |
| ----- | ----------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| 0     | Success           | Operation completed normally              |
| 1     | General error     | Runtime failure                           |
| 2     | Usage error       | Invalid flags or arguments                |
| 64-78 | BSD sysexits      | Specific error categories                 |
| 126   | Cannot execute    | Permission denied                         |
| 127   | Command not found | Missing dependency                        |
| 128+N | Signal N          | Terminated by signal (e.g., 130 = SIGINT) |

See [assets/examples/exit_codes.go](assets/examples/exit_codes.go) for a pattern mapping errors to exit codes.

## I/O Patterns

See [assets/examples/output.go](assets/examples/output.go) for all I/O patterns:

- **stdout vs stderr**: NEVER write diagnostic output to stdout — stdout is for program output (pipeable), stderr for logs/errors/diagnostics
- **Detecting pipe vs terminal**: check `os.ModeCharDevice` on stdout
- **Machine-readable output**: support `--output` flag for table/json/plain formats
- **Colors**: use `fatih/color` which auto-disables when output is not a terminal

## Signal Handling

Signal handling MUST use `signal.NotifyContext` to propagate cancellation through context. See [assets/examples/signal.go](assets/examples/signal.go) for graceful HTTP server shutdown.

## Shell Completions

Cobra generates completions for bash, zsh, fish, and PowerShell automatically. See [assets/examples/completion.go](assets/examples/completion.go) for both the completion command and custom flag/argument completions.

## Testing CLI Commands

Test commands by executing them programmatically and capturing output. See [assets/examples/cli_test.go](assets/examples/cli_test.go).

Use `cmd.OutOrStdout()` and `cmd.ErrOrStderr()` in commands (instead of `os.Stdout` / `os.Stderr`) so output can be captured in tests.

## Common Mistakes

| Mistake | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| Writing to `os.Stdout` directly | Tests can't capture output. Use `cmd.OutOrStdout()` which tests can redirect to a buffer |
| Calling `os.Exit()` inside `RunE` | Cobra's error handling, deferred functions, and cleanup code never run. Return an error, let `main()` decide |
| Not binding flags to Viper | Flags won't be configurable via env/config. Call `viper.BindPFlag` for every configurable flag |
| Missing `viper.SetEnvPrefix` | `PORT` collides with other tools. Use a prefix (`MYAPP_PORT`) to namespace env vars |
| Logging to stdout | Unix pipes chain stdout — logs corrupt the data stream for the next program. Logs go to stderr |
| Printing usage on every error | Full help text on every error is noise. Set `SilenceUsage: true`, save full usage for `--help` |
| Config file required | Users without a config file get a crash. Ignore `viper.ConfigFileNotFoundError` — config should be optional |
| Not using `PersistentPreRunE` | Config initialization must happen before any subcommand. Use root's `PersistentPreRunE` |
| Hardcoded version string | Version gets out of sync with tags. Inject via `ldflags` at build time from git tags |
| Not supporting `--output` format | Scripts can't parse human-readable output. Add JSON/table/plain for machine consumption |

ARGUMENTS: Analysing intropy-cli for mono-repo support: multiple scaffolded projects (each with .intropy/scaffold.json and skills.json) in one repository; need guidance on command structure, project discovery/selection flags, and workspace-style patterns

## TL;DR

The CLI is already *mostly* mono-repo-safe by design: every scaffolded project is self-contained (`.intropy/scaffold.json` + its own `skills.json`), and `manifests create` / `skills *` find their project by walking **up** from the current directory, so nearest-project-wins works today as long as you `cd` in. What's missing is everything that operates **across or from above** the projects: targeting a project without `cd`, enumerating projects, running a command over all of them, and guarding against the walk-up escaping a project's boundary. Those are the four things I'd add.

## What works today

- **`int create` is layout-agnostic.** `-n orders` scaffolds into `./orders` wherever you stand, so `repo/integrations/orders`, `repo/integrations/invoices` etc. just works. Crucially, `skillProjectAt` (`cmd/intropy/int_create_skills.go:115`) deliberately roots the skills project *exactly* at the new directory and never walks up — the comment even says "the scaffolded integration is its own skills project even when created inside a larger repo". Someone already thought about this.
- **Per-project records are self-contained.** `scaffold.json` carries blueprint, owner/repo, version, and values — no repo-level state, no shared config file to fight over.
- **Nearest-wins resolution.** `blueprint.FindScaffold` (`internal/blueprint/scaffold.go:69`) and `skill.FindProject` (`internal/skill/project.go:20`) both walk up to the first match, so from anywhere inside `orders/` you get `orders`' context. `manifests create` then defaults output to `<projectRoot>/deploy`, which is the right per-project answer.

## The gaps

**1. No way to target a project without `cd`-ing into it.** `deploy.CreateOptions.StartDir` exists internally but isn't exposed as a flag. In a mono-repo, CI pipelines and scripts want `intropy -C integrations/orders manifests create`, not `cd`-juggling.

**2. No enumeration.** There's no command that answers "which scaffolded projects live in this repo?" — the primitive a CI matrix build, a Backstage ingestion job, or an agent needs before fanning out.

**3. Confusing failure at the repo root.** Run `manifests create` at the mono-repo root and you get `ErrScaffoldNotFound` with a hint about *re-scaffolding* — misleading when three perfectly good projects sit one level down. The error assumes single-project repos.

**4. The skills walk-up can escape the project.** If someone runs `skills add` at the repo root once (which auto-bootstraps a `skills.json` in cwd, per the README), every later `skills add` from a subdirectory that happens to lack its own `skills.json` silently installs at the repo root. The walk-up has no boundary — it doesn't stop at `.git` or at another project's `.intropy/`.

## Suggestions, in priority order

**a) Add a persistent `-C <dir>` flag on the root command** (the `git -C` / `make -C` convention). Implementation is small: resolve it in the root's `PersistentPreRunE` and either `os.Chdir` or thread it as `StartDir` into the option structs — `deploy.CreateOptions` already has the field. This alone makes the CLI fully scriptable in a mono-repo:

```sh
for p in $(intropy int list -o json | jq -r '.[].path'); do
  intropy -C "$p" manifests create --no-input -f "$p/deploy-values.yaml"
done
```

**b) Add `intropy int list`** — walk *down* from cwd (or the git root), collect every `.intropy/scaffold.json`, print a table of path / blueprint / version, with `-o json` for machines. Skip `.git`, `node_modules`, `bin`, `dist`, and don't descend into a directory once it's matched (projects don't nest). This is the discovery primitive; everything else composes on top of it.

**c) Improve the not-found error with a downward scan.** When the walk-up fails, do a bounded scan below cwd and, if projects are found, say so: *"no scaffold.json here, but found 3 scaffolded projects: Demo/, Orders/, … — run with -C <dir> or cd into one."* Cheap, and it converts the most common mono-repo confusion into a self-explaining moment.

**d) Bound the walk-ups at the repo boundary.** Stop both `FindScaffold` and `FindProject` when the directory contains `.git` and nothing matched — matching there is fine, but walking *past* the repo root into `$HOME` never finds anything intentional. For the skills case specifically, consider also stopping the `skills.json` walk-up when a directory contains `.intropy/scaffold.json` but no `skills.json` — that directory *is* a project boundary, and bootstrapping there beats silently installing into a parent.

**What I'd deliberately skip (for now): a workspace file and a built-in fan-out command.** A `.intropy/workspace.json` at the root, or `manifests create --all`, adds state and partial-failure semantics (what happens when project 3 of 5 needs an interactive prompt?) for something `int list -o json` + a shell loop or a CI matrix already does deterministically. Convention-over-config: the repo layout *is* the workspace, discovered by scanning for `scaffold.json`. If fan-out demand becomes real, add it later on top of the list command — the composition order stays right.

One caveat on skills duplication: with one project per integration, each gets its own `.agents/skills` copy of the collection. I'd accept that — independent versioning per integration is a feature, and `skills.json` already supports `additionalBasePaths` if a team truly wants a shared install location.

Separately: your working tree has the whole `manifests create` feature plus the scaffold-record work sitting uncommitted (`scaffold.go`, `deploy/`, `manifests*.go`, the README section). That's a coherent unit — worth committing before starting mono-repo changes so the diffs stay separable.
How would you imagine that we will use the -C option?

Concretely, I'd expect `-C` to earn its keep in four places, roughly in this order of frequency:

**1. The Docker image you just shipped for CI and Backstage.** This is the strongest case. When the CLI runs as a container entrypoint — `docker run -v $PWD:/work intropy-cli intropy manifests create` — there is no shell, so there is no `cd`. Today the only options are baking `WORKDIR` decisions into the pipeline or wrapping everything in `sh -c "cd … && intropy …"`. With the flag it's just:

```sh
docker run -v "$PWD:/work" intropy-cli \
  intropy -C /work/integrations/orders manifests create --no-input -f deploy-values.yaml
```

Same story for a Backstage scaffolder/action step, which executes single-shot commands from a fixed workspace directory.

**2. CI matrix builds over the mono-repo.** The pipeline discovers projects once (`intropy int list -o json`), then each matrix job runs from the repo checkout root with its project as a parameter:

```yaml
strategy:
  matrix:
    project: ${{ fromJson(needs.discover.outputs.projects) }}
steps:
  - run: intropy -C ${{ matrix.project }} manifests create --no-input -f deploy-values.yaml
```

The job's cwd stays at the checkout root, so cache paths, artifact uploads, and everything else in the job keeps working unmodified — that's the real value over `cd` here.

**3. Agent and script fan-out.** Tool-executed commands (Claude Code, Taskfiles at the repo root, plain shell loops) are cleanest as single stateless invocations. `cd orders && intropy skills update --all` is a compound command that mutates shell state and trips permission allowlists; `intropy -C orders skills update --all` is one predictable command. A root Taskfile gets one-line per-project tasks without `dir:` blocks.

**4. Human one-offs from the repo root.** You're at the root reviewing a PR and want to regenerate one project's manifests or bump its skills — `intropy -C Orders skills update --all` without losing your shell context. Real, but the minor case.

One semantic decision to make before implementing: I'd give it **`git -C` semantics — behave exactly as if the process started in that directory** — rather than "just seed the scaffold walk-up". That means relative `-f values.yaml`, `-o`, and `--output-json` paths all resolve against the `-C` directory. That's what the matrix-build case wants (each project carries its own `deploy-values.yaml`), it's one `os.Chdir` in the root command's `PersistentPreRunE` instead of threading `StartDir` through every option struct, and it matches the convention people already know. The one gotcha — a shared root-level values file needs `-f ../shared-values.yaml` — is the same gotcha git users already understand, and one line in the README covers it.
